blocks.content:
High Courts can issue writs for:
• Enforcement of Fundamental Rights
• Enforcement of other legal rights

Important Difference:
• Supreme Court – Article 32 (only Fundamental Rights)
• High Court – Article 226 (Fundamental Rights + other rights)
High Court – Article 226 (Fundamental Rights + other rights)

items: Remember: High Court's writ jurisdiction under Article 226 is wider than the Supreme Court's writ jurisdiction under Article 32.
Supreme Court can issue writs ONLY for Fundamental Rights, whereas High Courts can issue writs for both Fundamental Rights and other legal rights.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: High Courts derive their authority to issue writs from Article 226.
High Courts can issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights as well as ordinary legal rights.
Supreme Court can issue writs under Article 32 strictly for Fundamental Rights only.
